title: Meghalaya Escape: Waterfalls & Living Roots
summary: Explore misty pine hills in Shillong, deep plunge waterfalls in Cherrapunji, crystalline waters of Umngot River in Dawki, and ancient Living Root Bridges.
gallery: /images/Meghalaya/Cherrapunjee/Double Decker Root Bridge/Double Decker Root Bridge.jpg
highlights: Walk beneath India's highest plunge waterfall — Nohkalikai
Glide on glass-like emerald waters at Umngot River, Dawki
Trek to the bio-engineered Double Decker Living Root Bridge in Nongriat
Stroll through Mawlynnong, celebrated as Asia's cleanest village
Experience Shillong's colonial cafes and vibrant local music culture

itinerary.title: Guwahati to Shillong via Umiam Lake
itinerary.description: Warm welcome at Guwahati. Drive uphill towards Shillong with a scenic photo break at the vast Umiam Lake. Evening exploration of Police Bazar and cafes.
itinerary.stay: Shillong boutique hotel or heritage homestay

itinerary.title: Shillong to Cherrapunji (Sohra) via Elephant Falls
itinerary.description: Morning visit to Elephant Falls and Shillong Peak. Journey across misty gorge roads into Sohra. Explore Mawsmai limestone caves, Seven Sisters Falls, and dramatic Nohkalikai viewpoint.

itinerary.title: Double Decker Living Root Bridge Trek or Wei Sawdong
itinerary.description: Early descent into Nongriat valley to witness the multi-tier living root architecture, or take an easier guided trail to Wei Sawdong three-tier cascade and Garden of Caves.

itinerary.title: Cherrapunji to Dawki & Mawlynnong, Return to Shillong
itinerary.description: Head down to Dawki near the Bangladesh border for country boat rides on the crystal-clear Umngot River. Visit Mawlynnong village and the single living root bridge at Riwai before driving back to Shillong.

itinerary.title: Shillong to Guwahati & Departure
itinerary.description: Optional morning stop at Don Bosco Museum or Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati before on-time airport drop with lifetime memories.

stayOptions: Handpicked 3-star boutique hotels and comfortable cliffside homestays with hot water and local breakfast included.
vehicleOptions: Innova Crysta for premium comfort (6 pax)
inclusions: All transfers & sightseeing in dedicated private vehicle as per group size
4 nights accommodation on twin-sharing basis with daily breakfast
Fuel, road taxes, interstate permits, parking, and driver allowances
Country boat ride on Umngot River in Dawki
Guwahati airport pickup and dropoff
exclusions: Airfare or train tickets to/from Guwahati
Lunches, dinners, and personal beverages

Trekking porter or personal gear hire
Anything not mentioned under inclusions
practicalNotes: Carry sturdy walking shoes for root bridge steps, light woollens for chilly Shillong evenings, and rain gear. Meghalaya is plastic-conscious; please avoid single-use plastics.

faqs.q: What is the best season for clear water at Dawki?
faqs.a: Water clarity is highest from November through April. Monsoon brings lush roaring waterfalls but causes river water to turn brownish.

faqs.q: Is the Double Decker Root Bridge trek suitable for elders?
faqs.a: The Nongriat trek involves approx 3,500 stone steps each way and requires moderate fitness. For seniors or guests with knee conditions, we arrange scenic alternative waterfall viewpoints.

title: Tawang Discovery: High Passes & Monasteries
summary: Ascend from subtropical Assam into the snow-crowned Eastern Himalayas, crossing 13,700-ft Sela Pass to reach Asia's second-oldest Buddhist monastery in Tawang.
highlights: Traverse the iconic Sela Pass (13,700 ft) beside frozen Sela Lake
Visit the 400-year-old Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
High-altitude excursion to Madhuri Lake (Sangetsar) and Indo-China Bum La Pass
Pay homage at Jaswant Garh War Memorial on the Himalayan ridge
Marvel at roaring Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)

itinerary.title: Guwahati to Bhalukpong / Nameri
itinerary.description: Drive northeast crossing the Brahmaputra River. Enter Arunachal Pradesh checkpost after permit verification and halt beside the Jia Bhoreli river.
itinerary.stay: Eco-resort in Bhalukpong or Dirang valley

itinerary.title: Bhalukpong to Dirang Valley
itinerary.description: Scenic climb through Kameng river gorge. Visit Dirang Dzong heritage village, apple orchards, and LDL Buddhist monastery atop the mountain hill.

itinerary.title: Dirang to Tawang via Sela Pass & Jaswant Garh
itinerary.description: Ascend to Sela Pass at 13,700 ft with prayer flags fluttering over Sela Lake. Stop at Jaswant Garh War Memorial and spectacular Nuranang Falls before reaching Tawang.

itinerary.title: Tawang Monastery, Urgelling & War Memorial
itinerary.description: Immerse in spiritual peace at Tawang Monastery, birthplace of 6th Dalai Lama at Urgelling Gompa, and attend the evening light & sound show at Tawang War Memorial.

itinerary.title: Bum La Pass & Madhuri Lake Excursion
itinerary.description: Board authorized local Arunachal 4x4 vehicle to reach Bum La (Indo-China border at 15,200 ft) and stunning Sangetsar Lake surrounded by fallen pine trees.

itinerary.title: Tawang to Bomdila
itinerary.description: Descend via Sela Pass towards Bomdila. Visit Bomdila Monastery with panoramic views of the Kangto and Gorichen snow peaks.

itinerary.title: Bomdila to Guwahati Departure
itinerary.description: Early departure descending through Assam tea gardens into Guwahati Airport for evening flights.

stayOptions: Clean, heated 3-star category hotel rooms with attached bathrooms and traditional Monpa hospitality.
vehicleOptions: Toyota Innova Crysta (highly recommended for mountain clearance)
inclusions: Private commercial vehicle throughout the itinerary from Guwahati
6 nights hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner included
Inner Line Permit (ILP) documentation assistance for Indian citizens
Driver mountain allowance, night charges, tolls, and fuel

exclusions: Bum La Pass & Madhuri Lake local union 4x4 vehicle fee (approx ₹5,500 per cab shared)
Military permit processing fee for border sector
Airfare and railway tickets
Lunches, personal tips, and heating extras where billed separately
practicalNotes: Indian nationals require an Inner Line Permit (ILP), which we arrange in advance. Foreign nationals require a Protected Area Permit (PAP) for minimum 2 persons. Bring warm down jackets and high-SPF sunscreen.

faqs.q: Is Bum La Pass open all year round?
faqs.a: Bum La is subject to military permissions and snow clearance. It typically remains accessible from April through mid-December, and intermittently in winter.

faqs.q: What vehicle is recommended for Tawang?
faqs.a: Toyota Innova Crysta or high-ground-clearance SUVs are strongly advised for comfort across Sela Pass road conditions.

title: Assam Wildlife: Kaziranga Rhino & Brahmaputra
summary: Spot the rare Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros in the floodplains of Kaziranga, cruise the sacred Brahmaputra River, and visit sacred Kamakhya Temple.
highlights: Private 4x4 Jeep Safari across Kaziranga Central and Western Ranges
Witness one-horned rhinos, wild water buffaloes, and migratory water birds
Evening traditional Bihu cultural dance performance at orchid park
Sunset river cruise on the mighty Brahmaputra River in Guwahati
Darshan at the venerable Kamakhya Devi Shakti Peetha

itinerary.title: Guwahati Arrival & Sunset Brahmaputra Cruise
itinerary.description: Arrive in Guwahati. Check into hotel and relax. In the late afternoon, embark on a serene river cruise on the Brahmaputra with folk music and river sunset views.

itinerary.title: Guwahati to Kaziranga National Park
itinerary.description: Morning drive through the fertile Brahmaputra valley lined with lush Assam tea estates. Check into your wildlife resort. Afternoon visit to Kaziranga National Orchid and Biodiversity Park.

itinerary.title: Kaziranga Jeep Safaris & Tea Estate Walk
itinerary.description: Morning open 4x4 Jeep safari into Bagori (Western) range with high rhino density. Afternoon safari into Kohora (Central) range for wetland birding and elephant herds.

itinerary.title: Kaziranga to Kamakhya Temple & Guwahati Departure
itinerary.description: Return drive to Guwahati. Visit Kamakhya Temple atop Nilachal Hill before timely transfer to Guwahati airport for your onward flight.

stayOptions: Handpicked eco-lodges and comfortable wildlife resorts situated right along the Kaziranga forest buffer zone.
inclusions: Guwahati to Kaziranga and return private transport
3 nights accommodation with daily breakfast
2 open 4x4 Jeep safaris into Kaziranga National Park with forest guide
Forest entry permits, camera toll, and vehicle safari fees
Sunset Brahmaputra river cruise ticket
exclusions: Elephant safari booking (optional add-on, subject to forest department lottery)
VIP Kamakhya special queue pass (purchased directly at temple)
Meals not specified in inclusions
Gratuities for safari driver and forest naturalist
practicalNotes: Kaziranga safari season operates strictly from October 15th to May 15th. Carry binoculars and earth-toned clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for game drives.

faqs.q: When is Kaziranga National Park open for safaris?
faqs.a: The park operates from mid-October to mid-May. Monsoon inundations close the park between June and late September.

faqs.q: Can we arrange an elephant safari?
faqs.a: Yes, elephant safaris are subject to daily forest department slot allocation. We assist guests with slot requests upon booking confirmation.

title: Dzukou Valley Trek: The Enchanted High Meadow
summary: Trek through bamboo forests and mountain passes into the mystical, rolling emerald ridges of Dzukou Valley, nestled at 8,000 feet on the Nagaland-Manipur frontier.
highlights: Hike the Viswema / Jakhama trail through misty highland rhododendron forests
Camp under pristine star-studded skies inside Dzukou Valley basin
Witness sunrise over rolling hillocks and serpentine crystal streams
Explore Kohima War Cemetery and vibrant Naga heritage village Kisama
Support local Angami Naga mountain guides and community eco-tourism

itinerary.title: Arrival in Dimapur & Transfer to Kohima / Kigwema
itinerary.description: Meet team at Dimapur Airport / Railway Station. Ascend through Naga hills into Kigwema village near the trailhead. Gear check and briefing.

itinerary.title: Trek to Dzukou Valley via Viswema Trailhead
itinerary.description: 4x4 vehicle drop to Viswema trailhead. Climb steep stone stairs to the valley rim, then enter the flat, rolling bamboo meadows of Dzukou. Settle at rest house / campsite.
itinerary.stay: Dzukou Rest House dormitory or high-altitude tents

itinerary.title: Full Day Exploring the Valley Basin, Caves & Streams
itinerary.description: Descend into the valley floor. Walk beside pristine streams, explore ghost caves, photograph rare flora (Dzukou Lily during bloom season), and witness dramatic sunset.

itinerary.title: Descend to Jakhama & Kisama Heritage Village
itinerary.description: Morning descent via the scenic Jakhama route. Transfer to Kisama Heritage Village (home of the Hornbill Festival) and relax in Kohima.

itinerary.title: Kohima War Cemetery & Drop to Dimapur
itinerary.description: Visit the historic Kohima War Memorial commemorating the Battle of Kohima 1944. On-time drop to Dimapur Airport / Railway Station for departure.

stayOptions: Cozy village homestays in Kigwema/Kohima and rustic mountain resthouse dormitories / alpine tents in the valley basin.
vehicleOptions: Dedicated Sumo / Bolero 4x4 for hill roads and trailhead transfer
inclusions: Dimapur roundtrip transfers and trailhead drops
2 nights village homestay/hotel and 2 nights valley camping/resthouse
Experienced Angami local mountain guide and trek leader
Dzukou Valley entry fees and indigenous community sanitation levy
Nutritious camp meals (breakfast and dinner) in the valley
exclusions: Personal porter for backpack (available on pre-booking at approx ₹1,500/day)
Sleeping bag / mat hire (available on request)
Lunch on transit days and snacks
Air/train tickets
practicalNotes: The valley has zero mobile connectivity and basic mountain toilet facilities. Trekkers must carry their own trash back down ('Leave No Trace' policy strictly enforced). Minimum age recommendation is 12 years.

faqs.q: When does the Dzukou Lily bloom?
faqs.a: The endemic Lilium chitrangadae blooms between late June and early August during the monsoon, coating the valley in pink-purple hues.

faqs.q: How cold does it get in Dzukou Valley?
faqs.a: Between November and February, night temperatures routinely dip below freezing (0°C to -3°C). Good thermal base layers and sub-zero rated sleeping bags are essential.
